title: From Scratch to SOTA: Training a 3B State-Space Vision Model — Krishna Prasad Srinivasan, Sarvam
talk_summary: Sarvam trained a 3B state-space (SSM) vision-language model from scratch for Indic document OCR, using a four-stage curriculum (text pretraining, vision continual pretraining, SFT, RLVR) plus a synthetic/real data engine and curated evals. The transferable ideas are architectural (small specialized models + harness modules, linear-cost SSMs for long inputs) and process (machine-verifiable rewards, eval-driven data loops), not the training itself.

takeaways.technique: Small specialized model + harness instead of one monolith
takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than one large VLM doing page-level OCR, they use a small 3B block-level model wrapped in layout and reading harness modules, doing lossy block-level recall to avoid full-page cost.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we at the time took a contrarian bet to focus on block level OCR instead adding a document hardness around the model
takeaways.numbers: 3B params; beats models ~100x larger on their benchmarks

takeaways.technique: Linear-cost sequence model for long inputs
takeaways.what_they_do: They chose an SSM over a transformer because attention compute grows quadratically with sequence length while SSM state/memory stays constant, which matters for 5-10k-token pages.
takeaways.evidence_quote: for long documents in particular which can lead up to uh uh 5 to 10,000 uh visual tokens per page and quadratic complexity

takeaways.what_they_do: Because OCR correctness is machine-checkable, they sample a group, score with unit tests, reinforce above-average outputs, and repeat — making RL scalable without human labels.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Sample a group, score with unit tests, reinforce what the average uh uh value to beat is, and then repeat the process

takeaways.what_they_do: They built pipelines to synthesize data and continuously improve training data based on eval performance, treating the data layer and eval layer as the real moat.

takeaways.technique: Confidence scores + block-level grounding for human-in-the-loop
takeaways.what_they_do: Their agentic workbench surfaces confidence scores and block-level grounding so humans can proofread and correct specific spans rather than re-doing whole documents.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We provide confidence scores um and we uh have block level grounding and then also the ability to do uh agentic proof reading

takeaways.what_they_do: They sequence capability building in stages (language prior first, then vision, then task SFT, then RL) so each stage builds on a strong prior instead of training everything at once.
takeaways.evidence_quote: four stages each uh building on the last
